text:
elaine: FYI — Centauri Health (enterprise) asked if we can be a drop-in for their current vendor (HeliosAPI). They want minimal client changes, same prompt/response shapes, and a security checklist answered by EOW. can we do a POC?
max: short answer: yes, but there are a few gotchas (param names, streaming framing, rate-limit semantics). need to scope acceptance criteria.
sam: +1. we should map their typical request/response examples and run our eval harness to check prompt parity. some endpoints use `x-request-id` and expect 200 with specific error body; we should replicate that in a compatibility shim.
mohit: can you paste a sample Helios payload? easier to propose adapter code with that.
elaine: pasted two sample payloads from customer below.
elaine: ```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "Summarize the note:",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "stream": true,
  "client_meta": {"tenant": "centauri-123"}
}
```
elaine: and their expected response frame (streaming):
elaine: ```
data: {"id":"r1","chunk":"..."}
data: {"error":null}
```
max: ok — differences to watch: 1) Helios uses `prompt` top-level vs our `input`/`messages` model; 2) their streaming frames are `data:` lines with JSON payloads (we can support that via a proxy that transforms our SSE to their framing); 3) rate-limit headers are `X-Helios-Limit` and they rely on `retry-after` semantics.
jordan: i can draft a short shim that translates request/response names + headers. we should confirm TLS client-certs? customer said they use mTLS for some endpoints.
alejandra: security note: Centauri requires answers to a subset of our enterprise questionnaire plus proof of SOC2 / encryption at rest / KMS integration. they also want an IP allowlist and audit log retention settings. i'll take the questionnaire. need an integration owner to fill the KMS/HSM details.
mohit: technical blocker: model output parity — Helios uses a custom tokenization and temperature scheduling that produces slightly different logits. we can tune by matching temperature/top_p and using same sampling seed for deterministic tests, but exact byte-for-byte parity is unlikely. need to surface that to the customer as an acceptance tolerance.
elaine: customer explicitly said "parity" but accepts prompt-level QA tests. their legal team insists on "no functional regressions for clinical summaries" — that will be the hard acceptance criterion.
max: propose POC plan: 1) build compatibility proxy that accepts Helios requests, maps to Redwood API, returns Helios-shaped responses. 2) run their canonical prompt set (we need ~200 clinical examples) through both systems, diff outputs with our eval scripts, produce a regression score. 3) address security items and confirm SLA/pricing. 4) short pilot for 2 weeks.
jordan: ETA for shim prototype ~3 business days if i get sample cURLs and token mapping.
elaine: sample cURL (customer):
elaine: ```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer HELIOS_TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"Summarize foo","max_tokens":256}' https://api.helios.ai/v1/generate
```
mohit: shim example (rough):
mohit: ```
# proxy snippet (python/fastapi)
@router.post('/v1/generate')
async def helios_to_redwood(payload: dict, authorization: str = Header(None)):
    # map prompt -> input/messages
    redwood_body = {"input": payload.get('prompt'), "max_tokens": payload.get('max_tokens')}
    # translate headers (x-request-id, client-meta -> metadata)
    resp = await call_redwood_api(redwood_body, api_key=map_token(authorization))
    # stream transform: wrap our streaming events into "data: {...}" frames the client expects
    return transform_stream(resp)
```
sam: thanks — also need to confirm our token mapping approach and whether we can accept their bearer tokens directly (we probably want to mint a short-lived internal token and map via an auth proxy). ops/security will need to sign off.
alejandra: we don't allow customer-supplied tokens on hosted infra. for Dedicated we can support mTLS and customer-managed tokens. for Hosted we can create an auth proxy that introspects and issues ephemeral tokens — i'll write the requirements.
elaine: pricing question from customer: they want a committed rate and to preserve their current per-req price for the first 6 months. sales: what levers do we have?
max: we can offer a short-term blended rate or a pilot discount tied to committed usage. also highlight cost improvements via batching and caching. need finance sign-off.
jordan: another gotcha — Helios returns some older error codes (422 for evaluation errors). client expects exactly those codes. shim will need to map Redwood error classes to Helios codes.
mohit: nondeterminism note: if we detect drift > threshold on eval harness, we can surface fallback to their previous vendor via routing policy for the pilot. avoids downtime risk.
elaine: asks: can eng-ml run an initial parity check on 50 examples this week? sam / mohit / max — can one of you run it?
sam: I can run the harness today — drop the 50 examples in the shared drive and tag me.
elaine: shared drive link: https://redwood-internal/company/centauri/prompt-set (customer shared)
jordan: I'll start the shim and post a deploy-bot message when the prototype is up.
deploy-bot: deploy started by jordan for branch shim/centauri-compat at commit abc123 — staging endpoint: https://staging-proxy.redwood.net/helios/v1/generate
jordan: staging up. sample test against customer cURL: passes basic mapping, streaming wrapper needs one bugfix (missing final end-of-stream frame).
mohit: running eval compares now, will post results in thread in ~2h.
elaine: thanks team — i'll consolidate answers to the security questionnaire and send the pilot SOW draft to the customer once we have the eval snapshot and pricing. :thumbsup:
